source: Standard exercises and programming. MET values from the 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities (Herrmann et al., J Sport Health Sci 2024).

how: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Sit your hips back and down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, chest up.
Push through your whole foot to stand.
squat-bw.safe: Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes, not caving in.
squat-bw.easy: Squat to a chair and stand back up.
squat-bw.hard: Pause 2 seconds at the bottom, or try jump squats.

how: Hands slightly wider than your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees to your body.
Press back up.
pushup.safe: Squeeze your glutes and abs so your hips don't sag.
pushup.easy: Hands on a counter or bench (incline push-up), or knees down.
pushup.hard: Feet raised on a step, or slow 3-second lowering.

how: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Lower with control.
glute-bridge.safe: Push through your heels and avoid arching your lower back at the top.
glute-bridge.hard: Single-leg bridge, or rest a dumbbell on your hips.

how: Stand tall, then step one foot back.
Lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, back knee just above the floor.
Push through the front heel to return. Alternate legs.
reverse-lunge.safe: Keep your front knee over your foot and your torso upright.
reverse-lunge.easy: Hold a chair or wall for balance and shorten the step.
reverse-lunge.hard: Hold dumbbells, or step back onto a cushion for less stability.

how: Take a long stride stance, back heel up.
Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive up through the front foot. Do all reps, then switch legs.
split-squat.safe: Move straight up and down; don't let the front knee collapse inward.
split-squat.hard: Rear foot on a bench (Bulgarian split squat).

how: Lean your back flat against a wall.
Slide down until your knees are bent about 90 degrees, feet under your knees.
Hold.
wall-sit.safe: Stop if you feel knee pain; slide up higher for an easier angle.
wall-sit.hard: Hold longer, or hold a dumbbell on your lap.

how: Stand on the edge of a step with your heels hanging off, holding a rail.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Lower your heels below the step slowly.
calf-raise.safe: Move slowly; don't bounce at the bottom.
calf-raise.hard: One leg at a time, or hold a dumbbell.

how: Forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
Body in one straight line from head to heels.
Brace your abs as if about to be poked, and breathe.
plank.safe: Stop when your hips start to sag or your back aches.
plank.hard: Lift one foot, or reach one arm forward.

how: Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, legs stacked.
Lift your hips so your body is straight.
Hold, then switch sides.
side-plank.safe: Keep your hips stacked and pushed forward, not sagging.

how: Lie on your back, arms straight up, knees bent at 90 degrees over your hips.
Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor while your lower back stays pressed down.
Return and switch sides.
dead-bug.safe: If your lower back lifts off the floor, shorten the reach.
dead-bug.hard: Hold a light dumbbell in each hand.

how: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your body.
Pause, return, switch sides.
bird-dog.safe: Keep your hips level; don't twist or arch.
bird-dog.easy: Move only an arm or only a leg.

how: Start in a high plank, hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs quickly, like running in place.
mountain-climber.safe: Keep your hips level with your shoulders.
mountain-climber.easy: Step the feet in slowly instead of running.

how: Jump your feet out wide while raising your arms overhead.
Jump back to the start.
jumping-jack.safe: Land softly on the balls of your feet.
jumping-jack.easy: Step one foot out at a time.
jumping-jack.hard: Go faster, or switch to burpees.

how: Run in place, driving your knees up to hip height.
Pump your arms.
high-knees.safe: Land softly and stay light on your feet.

how: Squat down to about parallel.
Jump up explosively.
Land softly and go straight into the next squat.
squat-jump.safe: Land with soft knees tracking over your toes.
squat-jump.easy: Regular squats, rising onto your toes.
squat-jump.hard: Pause at the bottom before jumping.

how: Start in a push-up, then walk your feet in and lift your hips into an upside-down V.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up.
pike-pushup.safe: Lower slowly and keep your neck neutral.

how: Hands on the edge of a sturdy bench or chair behind you, fingers forward, legs out in front.
Bend your elbows to lower your hips until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up.
bench-dip.safe: Stop if you feel shoulder pain; keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
bench-dip.easy: Bend your knees and keep your feet closer.
bench-dip.hard: Straight legs, or feet on another bench.

how: Hold a high plank with feet a little wider than hip-width.
Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, then switch, without rocking your hips.
shoulder-tap.safe: Widen your feet if your hips sway.

how: Lie face down, arms overhead.
Lift your arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor.
Hold 2 seconds and lower.
superman.safe: Lift only a little; keep your neck neutral.
superman.easy: Lift arms only, then legs only.

how: Squat and place your hands on the floor.
Jump or step your feet back to a plank.
Jump or step your feet back in and stand, reaching overhead.
burpee.safe: Step instead of jumping if your wrists or knees complain.
burpee.easy: Step back and forward with no jump or push-up.
burpee.hard: Add a push-up at the bottom.

how: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower all the way with control.
pullup.easy: Use a band or an assisted pull-up machine, or do slow lowering only.
pullup.hard: Add weight with a belt or a dumbbell between your feet.

how: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Squat down between your knees, elbows inside your knees, chest up.
Stand up through your whole foot.
goblet-squat.safe: Keep your heels down and your back flat.
goblet-squat.easy: Lighter weight, or squat to a box.

how: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and slide the weights down your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand.
db-rdl.safe: Keep your back flat and the weights close to your legs. Stop when your back starts to round.
db-rdl.easy: Lighter weights and a shorter range.

how: Lie on a bench with dumbbells over your chest, feet flat.
Lower them to the sides of your chest, elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
db-bench.safe: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down against the bench.
db-bench.easy: Do it on the floor (floor press).

how: Set the bench to about 30 degrees.
Lower the dumbbells to the top of your chest.
Press up and slightly together.
db-incline.safe: Don't let the weights drift too far apart at the bottom.

how: One hand and knee on a bench, back flat, dumbbell hanging from the other hand.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, elbow close to your body.
Lower slowly. Do all reps, then switch.
db-row.safe: Keep your back flat and don't twist your torso to lift.
db-row.hard: Pause with the weight at your hip for 2 seconds.

how: Hinge forward at the hips about 45 degrees, knees soft, a dumbbell in each hand.
Row both dumbbells toward your hips.
Lower with control.
db-bent-row.safe: Keep your back flat; stand more upright if you feel it in your lower back.

how: Seated or standing, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Press them overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower to shoulder height.
db-press.safe: Brace your abs and don't lean back.
db-press.hard: Standing, one arm at a time.

how: Stand with light dumbbells at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows slightly bent.
Lower slowly.
db-lateral.safe: Use light weights and don't shrug.

how: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Curl them up without moving your elbows forward.
Lower all the way.
Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other.
Curl up, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Lower slowly.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands overhead.
Bend your elbows to lower it behind your head.
Straighten your arms.
db-triceps.safe: Keep your elbows pointing forward and your ribs down.

how: Stand a stride in front of a bench and rest the top of your back foot on it, dumbbells at your sides.
Lower until your front thigh is about parallel.
Drive up through the front foot. Do all reps, then switch.
db-split.safe: Find a stance where your front knee stays over your foot.
db-split.easy: No weight, or a regular split squat.

how: Stand facing a sturdy bench or step, dumbbells at your sides.
Step up with one foot and drive through it to stand on the step.
Step down with control. Alternate or do one side at a time.
db-stepup.safe: Use a step height where your knee is no higher than your hip.

how: Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward and lower until both knees are about 90 degrees.
Push through the front foot and step into the next lunge.
db-lunge.safe: Keep your torso upright and steps long enough that your front knee stays over your foot.

how: Sit with your upper back against a bench, a dumbbell on your hips.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is flat from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes, then lower.
db-hipthrust.safe: Keep your chin tucked and ribs down so you don't arch your lower back.

how: Hinge forward with light dumbbells hanging below your chest.
Raise your arms out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly.
db-reardelt.safe: Use light weights and keep your back flat.

how: Lie face down on a bench set to about 30 degrees, dumbbells hanging down.
Row both dumbbells up toward your hips.
Lower slowly.
db-chest-row.safe: Keep your chest on the bench.

how: Pick up heavy dumbbells, one in each hand.
Walk tall with your shoulders back for the time or distance given.
Set them down with a flat back.
db-farmer.safe: Lift and lower the weights with your legs, not your back.

how: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders.
Squat down, then stand up explosively and use that drive to press the dumbbells overhead.
Lower them to your shoulders as you go into the next squat.
db-thruster.safe: Use light weights; keep your back flat at the bottom.

how: Hold dumbbells, balls of your feet on a step.
Rise as high as you can.
Lower your heels below the step slowly.
db-calf.safe: Hold a rail with one hand if you need balance.

how: Feet a little wider than your hips, kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
Hike it back between your legs, then snap your hips forward so it floats to chest height.
Let it fall back between your legs and repeat.
kb-swing.safe: It's a hip hinge, not a squat or an arm lift. Keep your back flat. Learn it with a light bell.

how: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at your chest.
Squat between your knees, chest up.
Stand up.
Kettlebell between your feet.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grab the handle.
Stand up by driving your hips forward.
kb-deadlift.safe: Keep the bell close and your back flat.
kb-deadlift.easy: Raise the bell on a step.

how: Hold the kettlebell at your shoulder, handle in your palm, bell resting on your forearm.
Press it straight overhead.
Lower with control. Do all reps, then switch.
kb-press.safe: Squeeze your glutes and don't lean back.

how: Staggered stance, one hand on a bench or your knee.
Row the kettlebell toward your hip.
Lower slowly. Switch sides.
Bar on your upper back, feet about shoulder-width.
Brace, then sit down between your hips until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive up, keeping your chest up.
bb-squat.safe: Squat inside a rack with the safety bars set just below your lowest point.
bb-squat.hard: Add weight gradually, about 5 lb per session while you can complete every rep.

how: Lie under the bar, eyes under it, feet flat, shoulder blades pulled back.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows about 45 degrees.
Press back up over your shoulders.
bb-bench.safe: Use safety arms or a spotter.

how: Hinge forward to about 45 degrees, bar hanging below your shoulders, back flat.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs.
Lower with control.
bb-row.safe: Keep your back flat; reduce the weight if your torso swings up.

how: Bar at your collarbones, hands just outside your shoulders.
Brace and press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Finish with the bar over your mid-foot.
bb-ohp.safe: Squeeze your glutes; don't lean back.

how: Bar over your mid-foot, hands just outside your legs.
Flatten your back, pull the slack out of the bar, and push the floor away until you're standing.
Lower by pushing your hips back, keeping the bar close.
bb-deadlift.safe: Your back must stay flat. Start light and learn the hinge before adding weight.

how: Hold the bar at your thighs, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down until you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand.
bb-rdl.safe: Keep your back flat and the bar touching your legs.

how: Upper back on a bench, padded bar across your hips.
Drive through your heels until your body is flat from shoulders to knees.
Lower with control.
bb-hipthrust.safe: Use a bar pad and keep your chin tucked.

how: Feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Lower until your knees are about 90 degrees.
Press back up without locking your knees.
leg-press.safe: Keep your lower back on the pad; don't go so deep that your hips curl up.

how: Knees lined up with the machine's pivot.
Straighten your legs.
Lower slowly.
leg-ext.safe: Use a weight you can control.

how: Knees lined up with the pivot, pad above your heels.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly.
leg-curl.safe: Keep your hips down on the pad.

how: Handles at mid-chest height.
Press forward until your arms are straight.
Return slowly.
chest-press-m.safe: Keep your shoulder blades against the pad.

how: Handles at shoulder height.
Press up until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly.
shoulder-press-m.safe: Keep your back against the pad.

how: Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders, thighs under the pads.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down.
Let it rise slowly.
lat-pulldown.safe: Don't lean far back or pull behind your neck.

how: Sit tall, feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle to your stomach, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Let your arms extend slowly.
seated-row.safe: Keep your back straight; don't rock.
seated-row.hard: Pause with the handle at your stomach.

how: Arms out wide, elbows slightly bent.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest.
Return slowly to a comfortable stretch.
pec-deck.safe: Don't let your arms go back further than is comfortable for your shoulders.

how: Rope or bar on a high cable.
Elbows at your sides, push the handle down until your arms are straight.
Let it rise until your forearms are about parallel to the floor.
Bar on a low cable.
Curl it up with your elbows at your sides.
Lower slowly.
Rope on a cable at face height.
Pull the rope toward your forehead, hands apart, elbows high.
Return slowly.
face-pull.safe: Use a light weight and move smoothly.

how: Kneel facing a high cable, holding the rope beside your head.
Curl your ribs toward your hips.
Return slowly.
cable-crunch.safe: Move from your abs, not your hips or arms.

how: Hips on the pad, feet secured.
Lower your upper body with a flat back.
Raise until your body is straight.
back-ext.safe: Don't arch past straight at the top.
back-ext.hard: Hold a weight plate at your chest.

how: Balls of your feet on the platform.
Rise as high as you can.
Lower your heels slowly for a full stretch.
Kneel or stand on the platform; more weight means more help.
Pull your chest toward the bar.
Lower slowly.
Walk at a pace where you can talk but not sing (about 3.5 mph).
Run at an easy, conversational pace.
jog.safe: Build up time gradually; increase your weekly running by no more than about 10%.

how: Set the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
bike.safe: Start each session with 5 easy minutes.

how: Push with your legs first, then lean back slightly, then pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Return in reverse: arms, body, then legs.
rower.safe: Keep your back straight; the power comes from your legs.

how: Stand tall and push and pull the handles as you stride.
Step at a steady pace, standing tall, hands resting lightly on the rails.
Swim steady laps of any stroke, resting at the wall as needed.
swim.hard: Swim continuously, or add sprint lengths.

how: Hold each stretch 20 to 30 seconds without bouncing: hamstrings, hip flexors, quads, chest, shoulders, upper back and calves.
stretch.safe: Stretch to mild tension, never pain.

how: Move slowly through cat-cow, downward dog, low lunge, child's pose and a supine twist, breathing steadily.
yoga.safe: Skip any pose that causes pain.

w.note: Can't do full push-ups yet? Do them with your hands on a counter. That still counts.
tips: Slow down: 2 seconds down and 1 second up makes bodyweight moves much more effective.
Stop each set when your form starts to slip, not when you can't move.
Do this three times a week and you'll notice push-ups and squats getting easier within a few weeks.
w.cheer: Every strong person started with the basics. Showing up today is the hard part.

w.note: Move from one exercise to the next with little rest. Rest 90 seconds after each round.
tips: Pick a pace you can hold for all three rounds. The first round should feel too easy.
Breathe out on the effort of each move, like standing up from the squat.
If you need to, pause briefly within a round; just keep moving between rounds.
w.cheer: Three rounds, no equipment, about 30 minutes. That's a real workout.

w.note: Warm up for 3 to 5 minutes first. Go hard during the work periods. Rest 1 minute between rounds.
tips: Warm up properly first. Intervals feel much better on warm muscles.
Hard means hard: aim for an effort where talking is difficult during the 40 seconds.
Swap jumps for the step versions if your knees or neighbors need a quieter day.
w.cheer: Twenty minutes, and the hardest part is the first round. You can do anything for 40 seconds.
w.metsrc: 02210 high intensity interval exercise, moderate effort

tips: Keep your weight in the middle of your foot on lunges and split squats.
Hold onto a wall or chair for balance. Your legs still do all the work.
Sore legs the next day are normal. Easy walking helps them recover.
w.cheer: Strong legs make everything easier, from stairs to carrying groceries.

tips: Incline push-ups on a counter are a smart way to build up to the floor.
Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back on every rep.
If your wrists bother you, do push-ups on your fists or holding dumbbell handles.
w.cheer: Your first full push-up is closer than you think. Every rep counts toward it.

tips: Quality beats speed: move slowly and keep your lower back steady.
Breathe throughout. Holding your breath doesn't make the plank stronger.
Add this after a walk or another workout two or three times a week.
w.cheer: A strong core protects your back in everything else you do. Fifteen minutes well spent.

tips: Pick dumbbells you could lift 2 more times at the end of each set. That's the right weight.
Write down your weights so next time you know when to go heavier.
Rest the full time between sets. It's part of the workout, not a break from it.
w.cheer: Full body in 40 minutes. Consistency with this beats any perfect program.

tips: On lunges, take a long enough step that your front knee stays over your foot.
Pause and squeeze at the top of each hip thrust.
Alternate this with workout A and you've trained everything twice in a week.
w.cheer: Workout B balances out A. Together they're a complete program.

tips: Start with the big presses and rows while you're fresh, and keep the arm work for the end.
Lower the dumbbells slowly; that's where much of the muscle building happens.
Go up in weight when you reach 12 reps on every set.
w.cheer: Upper body day. Strong shoulders and back make everyday life easier.

tips: Brace your abs before each rep of squats and Romanian deadlifts.
Bulgarian split squats are tough. Start with bodyweight to find your balance.
Walk around between sets to keep your legs loose.
w.cheer: Leg day is the one people skip, which is exactly why it pays off.

b: as many as you can with good form
tips: Keep your elbows about 45 degrees from your body on presses to keep your shoulders happy.
Use light dumbbells for lateral raises; the shoulders are small muscles.
Finish the push-ups with good form, even if that means only a few.
w.cheer: Chest, shoulders and arms. Leave a rep in the tank and come back stronger next time.

tips: Think about pulling with your elbows, not your hands, to feel your back work.
Keep your back flat on rows and Romanian deadlifts. Go lighter if it rounds.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of each row.
w.cheer: A strong back means better posture all day long. Nice choice.

tips: Go deep on the goblet squats with your chest up. Depth beats heavier weight.
Take the full rest on the big exercises so every set is good quality.
Stretch your hips and hamstrings afterward.
w.cheer: Big muscles, big payoff. Your legs burn the most calories of anything you train.

w.note: Use light to moderate dumbbells. Rest 90 seconds after each round.
tips: Choose dumbbells you could press 15 times fresh; fatigue makes them feel heavier fast.
Pace the first round so you can match it in the last.
Set the weights down whenever your form slips, take a breath, and continue.
w.cheer: Four rounds and you're done. Finish the last round as strong as the first.

w.note: Short on time? This hits every major muscle group in 20 minutes.
tips: Move straight from one exercise to the next to keep it at 20 minutes.
Even a short session keeps your streak and your strength going.
Busy days are exactly when a short workout matters most.
w.cheer: Twenty minutes counts. Short workouts done often beat long ones done rarely.

w.note: Learn the swing with a light kettlebell first. It's a hip hinge, not a squat.
tips: Practice the swing slowly first: a hip hinge with the kettlebell floating up, not lifted by your arms.
Keep the kettlebell close on goblet squats and rows.
If you're new to swings, film yourself once to check that your back stays flat.
w.cheer: Kettlebells build strength and conditioning at the same time. A great tool to learn.

tips: Fewer, better reps: rest fully and make every rep crisp.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of deadlifts and swings.
Move up a kettlebell size when the top of the rep range feels easy.
w.cheer: Steady, heavy and controlled. This is how you build real strength.

w.note: Warm up with an empty bar and a few lighter sets. When you finish all sets and reps with good form, add 5 lb next time.
tips: Warm up with the empty bar, then add weight in 2 or 3 jumps up to your work sets.
Set the safety bars in the rack before you squat or bench.
Log every session. Adding a little weight each time is the whole program.
w.cheer: Five sets of five. Simple, proven, and stronger every week.

w.note: One heavy set of deadlifts is enough after squats. Add 5 lb to squat and press, and 10 lb to deadlift, when you finish all reps.
tips: Learn the deadlift with light weight first; a flat back matters more than the number.
Brace like you're about to be poked in the stomach before every rep.
If the bar slows down a lot, end the set there. There's always next session.
w.cheer: Squat, press, deadlift. These lifts carry over to everything.

b: as many as you can (or assisted)
tips: Stop sets 1 or 2 reps before failure on the heavy barbell lifts.
Use a spotter or safety arms for the bench press.
If you can't do pull-ups yet, use the assisted machine or a band.
w.cheer: Heavy pressing and pulling. This is where upper body strength is built.

tips: Hit depth on squats before adding weight.
Keep the bar close to your legs on Romanian deadlifts.
Eat well afterward. Big leg sessions need fuel and protein to recover.
w.cheer: One of the toughest sessions in the program. Get through it and the rest of the week feels easier.

w.note: Machines guide the movement, which makes them a good place to start. Pick a weight where the last 2 reps feel hard.
tips: Adjust each machine so its pivot lines up with your joint, like the knee on the leg curl.
Pick a weight where the last two reps are hard but your form stays clean.
Most machines have a picture of how to use them. A quick look is worth it.
w.cheer: Machines are a great place to build strength safely and with confidence.

tips: Keep the movement slow and controlled; no swinging the weight stack.
Let the weight stack touch down lightly between reps without resting on it.
Alternate with workout A for a balanced week.
w.cheer: Every session adds up. You're building the habit as much as the muscle.

tips: Pull the lat pulldown bar to your upper chest, not behind your neck.
Keep the face pulls light and smooth; they're for shoulder health.
Increase the weight a little when you hit the top of the rep range on every set.
w.cheer: Upper body on machines, focused and efficient. Nicely done.

tips: Don't let your lower back peel off the leg press pad at the bottom.
Lower slowly on the leg extension and leg curl.
Finish with the cable crunches while your legs recover.
w.cheer: Leg day on machines: plenty of work, very little to go wrong.

tips: Bench first while you're fresh, then the dumbbell work.
Use a spotter or safety arms on heavy bench sets.
Take the lateral raises light and slow. Form over weight.
w.cheer: Push day. Pace yourself and keep 1 or 2 reps in reserve on the big lifts.

tips: Keep the Romanian deadlifts smooth and controlled. They're there to strengthen, not to max out.
Lead with your elbows on pulldowns and rows.
Grip giving out? Lifting straps are fine for the back exercises.
w.cheer: Pull day builds the back that holds everything else together.

tips: Warm up with a few lighter squat sets before your work sets.
Rest 2 to 3 minutes between squat sets. You'll lift more.
Hydrate and eat a solid meal with protein afterward.
w.cheer: Leg day. The hardest day of the split, and the one that pays off most.

tips: Alternate pressing and pulling to keep your shoulders balanced.
Keep a log so you can beat last week by a rep or a few pounds.
Stop sets with a rep or two left in the tank on heavy lifts.
w.cheer: Upper day done well. Strength is built a little at a time.

tips: Squat depth and a flat back come first; then add weight.
Use the full rest between heavy sets.
Gentle stretching afterward helps you feel better tomorrow.
w.cheer: Lower day. Big lifts, big progress.

w.note: Five of these a week covers the 150 minutes of moderate activity the US guidelines recommend.
tips: Walk briskly enough that you can talk but not sing.
Splitting it into three 10-minute walks counts just as much.
Swing your arms and stand tall; it naturally picks up the pace.
w.cheer: Walking is one of the best things you can do for your health, and it never gets old.

b: 60 s jog, then 90 s walk, 8 times
w.note: When this feels comfortable, jog longer and walk less, a little each week.
tips: Run slowly. If you can't talk in short sentences, slow down.
Finish wanting a little more, not completely spent.
Three sessions a week with a rest day between is the sweet spot.
w.cheer: Every runner started with intervals. You're building a habit one minute at a time.
w.metsrc: weighted from 17200 brisk walking (4.8) and 12020 jogging (7.5)

b: 24 min at a pace where you can talk
tips: Keep it conversational. Most of your running should feel easy.
Shorten your stride and let your feet land under you.
Increase your weekly running gradually, about 10% at a time.
w.cheer: Thirty minutes of running. That's an accomplishment worth being proud of.

b: 1 min hard, then 2 min easy, 5 times
tips: Set the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the stroke.
The hard minute should feel like an 8 out of 10. The easy 2 minutes are for recovering.
Easy on the knees, so it's a good choice on days your joints are tired.
w.cheer: Five hard minutes, spread out. You can do anything for one minute.

b: 14 min at a steady, moderate pace
tips: It's legs, then body, then arms. The power comes mostly from your legs.
Keep a steady rhythm rather than rowing fast with short strokes.
Sit tall and avoid hunching at the end of the stroke.
w.cheer: Rowing works almost every muscle you have. Twenty minutes well spent.

b: 30 min at a moderate, steady pace
tips: Stand tall and don't lean on the handles.
Raise the resistance a level every few minutes to keep it challenging.
